chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about palm trees and dates, when a man buys them for one year before they bear fruit. He said: 'No, until they bear fruit and their fruit is safe from defects. When they bear fruit, buy them for four years, if you wish, in addition to that year, or more than that, or less.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for selling unripe dates and palm fruit in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the prohibition of *Gharar* (uncertainty) in pre-harvest fruit sales by mandating that the fruit must first bear and be secure from defects before a valid transaction occurs. It further establishes the flexibility of the sale duration, allowing the buyer to acquire the produce for four years or a different agreed period, reflecting the practical agricultural realities of the time. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between speculative risk and legitimate commercial exchange in agricultural contracts.
